sanskrit: sa māṃsarudhiraughaiś ca medaughaiś ca samīritaḥ upary ākāśago vahnir vidhūmaḥ samadṛśyata
english: Fanned by floods of flesh and blood and streams of fat, the fire blazing above in the sky appeared smokeless.

sanskrit: dīptākṣo dīptajihvaś ca dīptavyāttamahānanaḥ dīptordhvakeśaḥ piṅgākṣaḥ piban prāṇabhṛtāṃ vasām
english: With blazing eyes, a blazing tongue, a blazing wide-open great mouth, blazing upright hair, and tawny eyes, he drank the marrow of living creatures.

sanskrit: tāṃ sa kṛṣṇārjunakṛtāṃ sudhāṃ prāpya hutāśanaḥ babhūva muditas tṛptaḥ parāṃ nirvṛtim āgataḥ
english: Obtaining that nectar-feast made for him by Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, the fire-god became joyful, satisfied, and attained supreme contentment.

sanskrit: athāsuraṃ mayaṃ nāma takṣakasya niveśanāt vipradravantaṃ sahasā dadarśa madhusūdanaḥ
english: Then Madhusūdana suddenly saw the asura named Maya fleeing in haste from the dwelling of Takṣaka.

sanskrit: tam agniḥ prārthayām āsa didhakṣur vātasārathiḥ dehavān vai jaṭī bhūtvā nadaṃś ca jalado yathā jighāṃsur vāsudevaś ca cakram udyamya viṣṭhitaḥ
english: The fire-god, wishing to burn him, with the wind as his charioteer, beseeched him, having taken on a bodily form with matted hair and roaring like a thundercloud; and Vāsudeva, wishing to kill him, stood with his discus raised.

sanskrit: sa cakram udyataṃ dṛṣṭvā didhakṣuṃ ca hutāśanam abhidhāvārjunety evaṃ mayaś cukrośa bhārata
english: Seeing the raised discus and the fire wishing to burn him, Maya cried out, "Run to Arjuna!" — thus, O Bharata.

sanskrit: tasya bhītasvanaṃ śrutvā mā bhair iti dhanaṃjayaḥ pratyuvāca mayaṃ pārtho jīvayann iva bhārata
english: Hearing his frightened cry, Dhanañjaya replied to Maya, saying "Fear not" — Pārtha, as if granting him life, O Bharata.

sanskrit: taṃ pārthenābhaye datte namucer bhrātaraṃ mayam na hantum aicchad dāśārhaḥ pāvako na dadāha ca
english: With Pārtha having granted him safety, the Dasharhaka did not wish to kill Maya, that brother of Namuci, and the fire did not burn him either.

sanskrit: tasmin vane dahyamāne ṣaḍ agnir na dadāha ca aśvasenaṃ mayaṃ cāpi caturaḥ śārṅgakān iti
english: While that forest burned, fire did not burn six beings: Ashvasena, Maya, and also the four Sharnagakas.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kimarthaṃ śārṅgakān agnir na dadāha tathāgate tasmin vane dahyamāne brahmann etad vadāśu me
english: Janamejaya said: Why did the fire not burn the Sharnagakas when the forest was burning thus, O brahmin? Tell me this quickly.

sanskrit: adāhe hy aśvasenasya dānavasya mayasya ca kāraṇaṃ kīrtitaṃ brahmañ śārṅgakānāṃ na kīrtitam
english: For the reason for the non-burning of Ashvasena and the danava Maya has been told, O brahmin, but the reason for the Sharnagakas has not been told.

sanskrit: tad etad adbhutaṃ brahmañ śārṅgānām avināśanam kīrtayasvāgnisaṃmarde kathaṃ te na vināśitāḥ
english: This is indeed wondrous, O brahmin — the non-destruction of the Sharnagas. Recount it: how were they not destroyed in the conflagration of the fire?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yadarthaṃ śārṅgakān agnir na dadāha tathāgate tat te sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ kathayiṣyāmi bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: For what reason the fire did not burn the Sharnagakas as it burned, I shall tell you everything just as it happened, O Bharata.

sanskrit: dharmajñānāṃ mukhyatamas tapasvī saṃśitavrataḥ āsīn maharṣiḥ śrutavān mandapāla iti śrutaḥ
english: Foremost among those who know dharma, an ascetic of sharp vows, a great seer learned in scripture, known as Mandapāla — such was he.

sanskrit: sa mārgam āsthito rājann ṛṣīṇām ūrdhvaretasām svādhyāyavān dharmaratas tapasvī vijitendriyaḥ
english: He followed the path of sages who preserve their seed upward, O king — devoted to sacred recitation, intent on dharma, an ascetic with conquered senses.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tapasaḥ pāraṃ deham utsṛjya bhārata jagāma pitṛlokāya na lebhe tatra tat phalam
english: Having reached the far shore of austerity and abandoning his body, O Bharata, he went to the world of the ancestors but did not obtain the expected fruit there.

sanskrit: sa lokān aphalān dṛṣṭvā tapasā nirjitān api papraccha dharmarājasya samīpasthān divaukasaḥ
english: Seeing those worlds to be fruitless even though won by austerity, he asked the celestials standing near the king of dharma.

sanskrit: kimartham āvṛtā lokā mamaite tapasārjitāḥ kiṃ mayā na kṛtaṃ tatra yasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam
english: Why are these worlds of mine, earned by austerity, closed to me? What have I not done such that this is the fruit of my deeds?

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ tat kariṣyāmi yadartham idam āvṛtam phalam etasya tapasaḥ kathayadhvaṃ divaukasaḥ
english: I shall do there whatever it is for which this fruit is blocked. Tell me, O celestials.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ ṛṇino mānavā brahmañ jāyante yena tac chṛṇu kriyābhir brahmacaryeṇa prajayā ca na saṃśayaḥ
english: The gods said: Men are born indebted, O brahmin — hear by what they discharge it: through ritual acts, through celibate study, and through offspring — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tad apākriyate sarvaṃ yajñena tapasā sutaiḥ tapasvī yajñakṛc cāsi na tu te vidyate prajā
english: All of it is discharged by sacrifice, by austerity, and by sons. You are an ascetic and a sacrificer, but you have no offspring.

sanskrit: ta ime prasavasyārthe tava lokāḥ samāvṛtāḥ prajāyasva tato lokān upabhoktāsi śāśvatān
english: Therefore these worlds of yours are closed for want of progeny. Beget children; then you shall enjoy eternal worlds.

sanskrit: punnāmno narakāt putras trātīti pitaraṃ mune tasmād apatyasaṃtāne yatasva dvijasattama
english: "A son delivers the father from the hell named Put" — thus it is said, O sage. Therefore strive for the continuation of offspring, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā mandapālas tu teṣāṃ vākyaṃ divaukasām kva nu śīghram apatyaṃ syād bahulaṃ cety acintayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing the words of those celestials, Mandapāla pondered: "Where can I quickly obtain abundant offspring?"

sanskrit: sa cintayann abhyagacchad bahulaprasavān khagān śārṅgikāṃ śārṅgako bhūtvā jaritāṃ samupeyivān
english: Reflecting thus, he approached the birds known for prolific reproduction; becoming a sharnaka bird himself, he came to Jarita.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ putrān ajanayac caturo brahmavādinaḥ tān apāsya sa tatraiva jagāma lapitāṃ prati bālān sutān aṇḍagatān mātrā saha munir vane
english: He begot four sons on her, versed in brahman. Abandoning them — those infant sons still within their eggs, along with their mother — the sage went off in that very forest to Lapita.

sanskrit: tasmin gate mahābhāge lapitāṃ prati bhārata apatyasnehasaṃvignā jaritā bahv acintayat
english: After that great one had gone to Lapita, O Bharata, Jarita, agitated by love for her children, pondered deeply.

sanskrit: tena tyaktān asaṃtyājyān ṛṣīn aṇḍagatān vane nājahat putrakān ārtā jaritā khāṇḍave nṛpa babhāra caitān saṃjātān svavṛttyā snehaviklavā
english: Abandoned by him though undeserving of abandonment — those young seers still in their eggs in the forest — the distressed Jarita did not forsake her little ones in Khandava, O king; she nurtured them as they were born, her heart overcome with love.

sanskrit: tato 'gniṃ khāṇḍavaṃ dagdhum āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭavān ṛṣiḥ mandapālaś caraṃs tasmin vane lapitayā saha
english: Then the sage Mandapāla, wandering in that forest with Lapita, saw the fire coming to burn Khandava.

sanskrit: taṃ saṃkalpaṃ viditvāsya jñātvā putrāṃś ca bālakān so 'bhituṣṭāva viprarṣir brāhmaṇo jātavedasam putrān paridadad bhīto lokapālaṃ mahaujasam
english: Understanding the fire's intention and knowing his infant sons were there, that brahmin sage, the seer Mandapāla, praised Jātaveda the mighty world-guardian with fear, entrusting his sons to him.

sanskrit: mandapāla uvāca tvam agne sarvadevānāṃ mukhaṃ tvam asi havyavāṭ tvam antaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ gūḍhaś carasi pāvaka
english: Mandapāla said: You are the mouth of all the gods, O fire; you are the carrier of oblations; you move secretly within all beings, O purifier.

sanskrit: tvām ekam āhuḥ kavayas tvām āhus trividhaṃ punaḥ tvām aṣṭadhā kalpayitvā yajñavāham akalpayan
english: The poets call you one; they also call you threefold. Having conceived you as eightfold, they ordained you as the vehicle of sacrifice.

sanskrit: tvayā sṛṣṭam idaṃ viśvaṃ vadanti paramarṣayaḥ tvad ṛte hi jagat kṛtsnaṃ sadyo na syād dhutāśana
english: The supreme seers declare this universe was created by you; for without you, O fire, the entire world could not exist for a moment.

sanskrit: tubhyaṃ kṛtvā namo viprāḥ svakarmavijitāṃ gatim gacchanti saha patnībhiḥ sutair api ca śāśvatīm
english: Brahmins who bow to you attain the eternal destination won by their own deeds, together with their wives and children.

sanskrit: tvām agne jaladān āhuḥ khe viṣaktān savidyutaḥ dahanti sarvabhūtāni tvatto niṣkramya hāyanāḥ
english: They call you, O fire, the cloud-givers suspended in the sky with lightning; the seasons that burn all beings issue forth from you.

sanskrit: jātavedas tavaiveyaṃ viśvasṛṣṭir mahādyute tavaiva karma vihitaṃ bhūtaṃ sarvaṃ carācaram
english: O Jātaveda, O greatly radiant one, this creation of the universe is yours alone; all being — both moving and unmoving — is decreed by your action alone.

sanskrit: tvayāpo vihitāḥ pūrvaṃ tvayi sarvam idaṃ jagat tvayi havyaṃ ca kavyaṃ ca yathāvat saṃpratiṣṭhitam
english: The waters were ordained by you from the beginning; in you all this world rests; in you oblations to the gods and offerings to the ancestors are properly established.

sanskrit: agne tvam eva jvalanas tvaṃ dhātā tvaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ tvam aśvinau yamau mitraḥ somas tvam asi cānilaḥ
english: O fire, you yourself are the flaming one; you are Dhata; you are Bṛhaspati; you are the twin Aśvins; you are Yama; you are Mitra; you are Soma; and you are the wind.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ stutas tatas tena mandapālena pāvakaḥ tutoṣa tasya nṛpate muner amitatejasaḥ uvāca cainaṃ prītātmā kim iṣṭaṃ karavāṇi te
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus praised by Mandapāla, the fire was pleased with that sage of boundless splendor, O king, and spoke to him with a gladdened heart: "What is your wish? What shall I do for you?"

sanskrit: tam abravīn mandapālaḥ prāñjalir havyavāhanam pradahan khāṇḍavaṃ dāvaṃ mama putrān visarjaya
english: Mandapāla, with joined palms, addressed the carrier of oblations: "While burning the Khandava forest, spare my sons."

sanskrit: tatheti tat pratiśrutya bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ khāṇḍave tena kālena prajajvāla didhakṣayā
english: Saying "So be it" and making that promise, the blessed fire-carrier blazed forth in Khandava at that time with the desire to burn.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prajvalite śukre śārṅgakās te suduḥkhitāḥ vyathitāḥ paramodvignā nādhijagmuḥ parāyaṇam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the bright fire blazed, those Sharnagakas were deeply grieved, tormented, and greatly distressed — they found no refuge.

sanskrit: niśāmya putrakān bālān mātā teṣāṃ tapasvinī jaritā duḥkhasaṃtaptā vilalāpa nareśvara
english: Seeing her infant children, their ascetic mother Jarita, scorched by grief, lamented, O lord of men.

sanskrit: ayam agnir dahan kakṣam ita āyāti bhīṣaṇaḥ jagat saṃdīpayan bhīmo mama duḥkhavivardhanaḥ
english: "This fire, terrible and fearsome, burning the undergrowth, comes here, setting the world ablaze, the augmenter of my sorrow."

sanskrit: ime ca māṃ karṣayanti śiśavo mandacetasaḥ abarhāś caraṇair hīnāḥ pūrveṣāṃ naḥ parāyaṇam trāsayaṃś cāyam āyāti lelihāno mahīruhān
english: "These infants, slow of mind, without tail-feathers, lacking the use of their feet — our ancient refuge — torment me; and this fire comes licking the great trees, terrifying us."

sanskrit: aśaktimattvāc ca sutā na śaktāḥ saraṇe mama ādāya ca na śaktāsmi putrān saritum anyataḥ
english: "Because of their helplessness, my sons are not capable of fleeing; and I cannot flee elsewhere while carrying my children."

sanskrit: na ca tyaktum ahaṃ śaktā hṛdayaṃ dūyatīva me kaṃ nu jahyām ahaṃ putraṃ kam ādāya vrajāmy aham
english: "Nor am I able to abandon them — my heart burns with pain. Which son shall I forsake? Taking which shall I go?"

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me syāt kṛtaṃ kṛtvā manyadhvaṃ putrakāḥ katham cintayānā vimokṣaṃ vo nādhigacchāmi kiṃ cana chādayitvā ca vo gātraiḥ kariṣye maraṇaṃ saha
english: "What would have been done being done — think, my little ones, how? Pondering your deliverance I find no way. Covering you with my body I shall die together with you."

sanskrit: jaritārau kulaṃ hīdaṃ jyeṣṭhatvena pratiṣṭhitam sārisṛkvaḥ prajāyeta pitṝṇāṃ kulavardhanaḥ
english: "This lineage of Jaritari is established by the eldest; Sarisrikva shall be born to increase the family of the ancestors."

sanskrit: stambamitras tapaḥ kuryād droṇo brahmavid uttamaḥ ity evam uktvā pitā vo nirghṛṇaḥ purā
english: "Stambamitra shall practice austerity; Droṇa shall be the supreme knower of brahman — saying thus, your father, pitiless one, departed long ago."

sanskrit: kam upādāya śakyeta gantuṃ kasyāpad uttamā kiṃ nu kṛtvā kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ bhaved iti ca vihvalā
english: "Carrying which can one go? For whom would flight be best? What, if done, would the duty be done?" — distracted thus she thought.

sanskrit: nāpaśyat svadhiyā mokṣaṃ svasutānāṃ tadānalāt evaṃ bruvantīṃ śārṅgās te pratyūcur atha mātaram
english: She could not find by her own wit any deliverance for her sons from that fire. As she spoke thus, those Sharnagas then replied to their mother.

sanskrit: sneham utsṛjya mātas tvaṃ pata yatra na havyavāṭ asmāsu hi vinaṣṭeṣu bhavitāraḥ sutās tava tvayi mātar vinaṣṭāyāṃ na naḥ syāt kulasaṃtatiḥ
english: "Casting aside affection, O mother, fly to where the fire-carrier cannot reach. When we are gone you shall have other sons; but if you perish, O mother, there shall be no continuation of our lineage."

sanskrit: anvavekṣyaitad ubhayaṃ kṣamaṃ syād yat kulasya naḥ tad vai kartuṃ paraḥ kālo mātar eṣa bhavet tava
english: "Consider both sides — what would be best for our lineage. That is what ought to be done; this, O mother, should be your supreme moment of action."

sanskrit: mā vai kulavināśāya snehaṃ kārṣīḥ suteṣu naḥ na hīdaṃ karma moghaṃ syāl lokakāmasya naḥ pituḥ
english: "Do not make your affection for us the cause of the lineage's ruin. This deed of our father who desired the worlds shall not be in vain."

sanskrit: jaritovāca idam ākhor bilaṃ bhūmau vṛkṣasyāsya samīpataḥ tad āviśadhvaṃ tvaritā vahner atra na vo bhayam
english: Jarita said: Here in the earth near this tree is the burrow of a mouse. Enter it quickly — there is no fear of the fire for you here.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ pāṃsunā chidram apidhāsyāmi putrakāḥ evaṃ pratikṛtaṃ manye jvalataḥ kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ
english: "Then I shall block the opening with dust, my little ones. Thus I think we may act against the blazing black-pathed fire."

sanskrit: tata eṣyāmy atīte 'gnau vihartuṃ pāṃsusaṃcayam rocatām eṣa vopāyo vimokṣāya hutāśanāt
english: "After the fire has passed I shall come back to scatter the mound of dust. Let this plan for your deliverance from the fire please you."

sanskrit: śārṅgakā ūcuḥ abarhān māṃsabhūtān naḥ kravyādākhur vināśayet paśyamānā bhayam idaṃ na śakṣyāmo niṣevitum
english: The Sharnagakas said: The flesh-eating mouse would destroy us who are featherless and without tail-plumage. We cannot resort to this plan, seeing this danger before us.

sanskrit: katham agnir na no dahyāt katham ākhur na bhakṣayet kathaṃ na syāt pitā moghaḥ kathaṃ mātā dhriyeta naḥ
english: "How might the fire not burn us? How might the mouse not devour us? How might our father not be in vain? How might our mother survive?"

sanskrit: bila ākhor vināśaḥ syād agner ākāśacāriṇām anvavekṣyaitad ubhayaṃ śreyān dāho na bhakṣaṇam
english: "In the burrow destruction would come from the mouse; from the fire, for those who fly in the sky. Weighing both sides: burning is better than being devoured."

sanskrit: garhitaṃ maraṇaṃ naḥ syād ākhunā khādatā bile śiṣṭād iṣṭaḥ parityāgaḥ śarīrasya hutāśanāt
english: "Death by being eaten by the mouse in the burrow would be shameful for us. More desirable than the shameful is the abandonment of the body in the fire."

sanskrit: jaritovāca asmād bilān niṣpatitaṃ śyena ākhuṃ jahāra tam kṣudraṃ gṛhītvā pādābhyāṃ bhayaṃ na bhavitā tataḥ
english: Jarita said: A hawk flew out from this very burrow and carried off that mouse, that small creature, gripping it with its talons. There will be no danger from it now.

sanskrit: śārṅgakā ūcuḥ na hṛtaṃ taṃ vayaṃ vidmaḥ śyenenākhuṃ kathaṃ cana anye 'pi bhavitāro 'tra tebhyo 'pi bhayam eva naḥ
english: The Sharnagakas said: We do not know in the least that the mouse was carried off by a hawk. And there may be others here — from them too we face danger.

sanskrit: saṃśayo hy agnir āgacched dṛṣṭaṃ vāyor nivartanam mṛtyur no bilavāsibhyo bhaven mātar asaṃśayam
english: "The fire may or may not come — we have seen the wind turn it back. But death for us from the burrow's inhabitants would be certain, O mother."

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayāt saṃśayito mṛtyur mātar viśiṣyate cara khe tvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ putrān vetsyasi śobhanān
english: "A doubtful death is better than a certain one, O mother. Go as is proper through the sky — you shall obtain splendid sons."

sanskrit: jaritovāca ahaṃ vai śyenam āyāntam adrākṣaṃ bilam antikāt saṃcarantaṃ samādāya jahārākhuṃ bilād balī
english: Jarita said: I myself saw the hawk coming, moving near the burrow; that powerful one seized the mouse and carried it off from the burrow.

sanskrit: taṃ patantam ahaṃ śyenaṃ tvaritā pṛṣṭhato 'nvagām āśiṣo 'sya prayuñjānā harato mūṣakaṃ bilāt
english: "That hawk as it flew I quickly followed behind, conferring blessings on it as it carried the mouse away from the burrow."

sanskrit: yo no dveṣṭāram ādāya śyenarāja pradhāvasi bhava tvaṃ divam āsthāya niramitro hiraṇmayaḥ
english: "O king of hawks, you who dash away carrying our enemy — may you become golden, foe-free, ascending the sky."

sanskrit: yadā sa bhakṣitas tena kṣudhitena patatriṇā tadāhaṃ tam anujñāpya pratyupāyāṃ gṛhān prati
english: "When it is devoured by that hungry bird, then, having taken leave of him, I shall return home."

sanskrit: praviśadhvaṃ bilaṃ putrā viśrabdhā nāsti vo bhayam śyenena mama paśyantyā hṛta ākhur na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Enter the burrow, my sons, with confidence — there is no danger for you. The mouse was carried off by the hawk while I watched — there is no doubt."

sanskrit: śārṅgakā ūcuḥ na vidma vai vayaṃ mātar hṛtam ākhum itaḥ purā avijñāya na śakṣyāmo bilam āviśatuṃ vayam
english: The Sharnagakas said: We do not know, O mother, whether the mouse was carried off from here before. Without knowing for certain we cannot enter the burrow.

sanskrit: jaritovāca ahaṃ hi taṃ prajānāmi hṛtaṃ śyenena mūṣakam ata eva bhayaṃ nāsti kriyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama
english: Jarita said: I know that the mouse was carried off by the hawk. Therefore there is no danger — do as I say.

sanskrit: śārṅgakā ūcuḥ na tvaṃ mithyopacāreṇa mokṣayethā bhayaṃ mahat samākuleṣu jñāneṣu na buddhikṛtam eva tat
english: The Sharnagakas said: You should not seek to rescue us by false comfort. In turbulent knowledge great fear is not subdued by mere reasoning.

sanskrit: na copakṛtam asmābhir na cāsmān vettha ye vayam pīḍyamānā bharasy asmān kā satī ke vayaṃ tava
english: "Nor have we done you any service, nor do you truly know who we are. You sustain us while we afflict you — what woman of virtue are you, and who are we to you?"

sanskrit: taruṇī darśanīyāsi samarthā bhartur eṣaṇe anugaccha svabhartāraṃ putrān āpsyasi śobhanān
english: "You are young and beautiful, capable of seeking a husband. Follow your own lord — you shall obtain splendid sons."

sanskrit: vayam apy agnim āviśya lokān prāpsyāmahe śubhān athāsmān na dahed agnir āyās tvaṃ punar eva naḥ
english: "We too, entering the fire, shall attain auspicious worlds. Or if the fire does not burn us, then come back to us again."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktā tataḥ śārṅgī putrān utsṛjya khāṇḍave jagāma tvaritā deśaṃ kṣemam agner anāśrayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Addressed thus, the sharnaga hen, abandoning her sons in Khandava, quickly departed to a safe place, a refuge from the fire.

sanskrit: tatas tīkṣṇārcir abhyāgāj jvalito havyavāhanaḥ yatra śārṅgā babhūvus te mandapālasya putrakāḥ
english: Then the fire-carrier blazed with sharp flames and came to where those Sharnagas were — the little sons of Mandapāla.

sanskrit: te śārṅgā jvalanaṃ dṛṣṭvā jvalitaṃ svena tejasā jaritāris tato vācaṃ śrāvayām āsa pāvakam
english: Those Sharnagas, seeing the blazing fire blazing with its own splendor, — Jaritari then caused the fire to hear his voice.
